==English==

===Alternative forms===
* {{alter|en|examin||obsolete}}

===Etymology===
From {{inh|en|enm|examinen}}, {{m|enm|examenen}}, from {{der|en|fro|examiner}}, from {{der|en|la|examino|exāmināre}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ɪɡˈzæmɪn/}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-examine.ogg|a=US}}
* {{hyphenation|en|ex|am|ine}}

===Verb===
{{wikidata lexeme|L113}}
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[observe]] [[careful]]ly or [[critical]]ly to learn about someone or something.
#: {{syn|en|canvass}}
#: {{ux|en|He '''examined''' the crime scene for clues.}}
#: {{ux|en|She '''examined''' the hair sample under a microscope.}}
#* {{quote-song|en|year=1979|album=w:Stay Free (album)|author=w:Ashford & Simpson|title=Nobody Knows|text=Well, nobody knows about the little things / Nobody knows what they really mean / Nobody ever wants to take the time / To '''examine''' what's on your mind}}
#* {{RQ:Schuster Hepaticae|volume=V|page=vii|text=With fresh material, taxonomic conclusions are leavened by recognition that the material '''examined''' reflects the site it occupied; a herbarium packet gives one only a small fraction of the data desirable for sound conclusions. Herbarium material does not, indeed, allow one to extrapolate safely: what you see is what you get{{...}}}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[check]] the [[health]] or [[condition]] of something or someone.
#: {{ux|en|The doctor '''examined''' the patient.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[determine]] the [[aptitude]], [[skill]]s or [[qualification]]s of someone by subjecting them to an [[examination]].
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[interrogate]].
#: {{ux|en|The witness was '''examined''' under oath.}}

====Synonyms====
* {{l|en|pore over}}, {{l|en|undersee}}

* {{l|en|re-examine}}
